hypothesis: Question: is the 0.09 RMSE development gain of idea-237111 (8.292 vs median 8.379, 7 patients) evidence of a transferable patient-level voice signal, or noise/demographics/transductive shrinkage? Prior evidence: idea-5c676c showed ~92% of motor_UPDRS variance is between patients and no row-level model beat a constant patient-held-out; idea-237111's 7-fold train candidates differ by only ~0.1-0.2 row RMSE (const 7.88, demo 7.95, mean_a1000 7.79, demo+mean+std 7.75) on 28 patients, which is inside plausible sampling noise, and its selection also depended on pseudo-grouping by rounded (age,sex) that merges patients. This moves me from 'which aggregate model' to 'is there any patient-level signal at all', which determines whether the remaining 3 rounds should attempt a >=5% method or select conservatively. Contrasting outcomes before execution: (A) signal exists: on the pooled 35 patients (train+dev, true groups) the voice-aggregate ridge LOO patient RMSE beats the constant with a permutation p<0.05 and a paired-bootstrap CI of row-RMSE difference excluding 0, and patient-level Spearman |r| of some mean voice feature exceeds the max-|r| permutation null q95; (B) no separable signal: permutation p>0.2, CIs straddle 0, and the development gain of idea-237111 is concentrated in one or two patients' bias, with demo-only and voice models giving similar per-patient biases. Also reports target structure (between-patient variance share, within-patient SD, per-day slope) to separate a patient-constant explanation from a drift explanation. Caveat: this analysis reads development labels (allowed in analyze), so it is diagnostic and any later choice informed by it is development-tuned; it produces no score and cannot by itself establish success.
